entry.title: Project "Surnames of the World"
entry.subtitle: Meta page for regional surname wordcloud posts
entry.excerpt: A navigation hub for regional surname wordcloud visualizations, with methodology notes and a legacy-style grid.
entry.content: This is a **meta-post** to ease navigation across surname wordcloud visualizations by world region. Political boundaries are mostly shown according to their “de facto” status. Raw data came from [Forebears.io](https://forebears.io/). ## Regions ## FAQ The bigger the word, the more frequent the surname. Wordclouds are built from aggregated surname frequencies by administrative unit. Interactive reference example: Apache ECharts wordcloud demo. ## References _Natural Earth’s editorial policy is to show political boundaries according to their de facto status. We show disputed areas and boundaries, too, so you can repurpose to suit your needs. This policy has been in place since the project launch in 2009._ [Natural Earth’s Disputed boundaries policy](https://www.naturalearthdata.com/about/disputed-boundaries-policy/) Good editorial use: move low-priority details (naming debates, one-off caveats, timeline precision) into notes so the main paragraph stays clear. - Forebears article (archived): “Accuracy of Surname Statistics on Forebears” - Naming customs: [FamilySearch Europe](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Europe)
